claude_isolation.what_that_means: install-codex.sh does not open, copy, move or delete anything under $HOME/.claude, and refuses a destination that resolves inside a Claude home. The combined install is additive: install-codex.sh --with-claude delegates to the unmodified install.sh rather than reimplementing it, so install.sh, package.json, .claude/** and evals/codex/baselines/ carry zero diff in this phase.

bindings.what_it_does: Installs the generated Codex tree into $HOME/.agents/skills and $HOME/.agents/scripts — the locations Codex discovers — mirroring the Claude installer's shape: source resolution (clone or --from), pre-install verification of the generated tree, copy-never-delete with an explicit retired-name sweep, executable-bit repair, and a version stamp written last because copying msg/ clears its destination first. The stamp carries `runtime: codex` so a machine holding both installs can say which tree answered. A --dest is refused if it resolves inside a Claude home.

Runs the unmodified install.sh for the Claude half after the Codex half succeeds, and suppresses its own cook bootstrap because install.sh already owns that flag. A failure in the Claude half is reported without unwinding the Codex install.

Closes the last coverage gap in the suite: the twelve SHR-CX assertions named by the shared compatibility map had no executing case before this phase. Eight cases now carry them — digest bijection, consumer-edge closure, the finding/report wire contract, the policy resolution matrix, safety and human gates, dispatch/watch/heartbeat, fix-loop ordering, and doctor/cache degradation — taking assertion coverage to 146 of 146.

Nine layer-3 cases, one per skill, each running four live Codex sessions from a clean thread in an isolated temporary home: a happy path, an ambiguous input, a refusal and a safety-sensitive path. Prompts are written as a user would write them — the expected answer is never supplied, and the skill name is only mentioned where a real user would mention it. Every session runs --sandbox read-only, so a forward test can consider shipping without any possibility of shipping. Each session leaves a raw event stream, a normalized semantic trace and its untruncated answer under evals/codex/forward/<skill>/.
bindings.grading: Semantic, not verbatim: whether the right skill was selected, whether an under-specified request was questioned rather than guessed at, whether an out-of-authority request was refused and handed on, and whether the workspace stayed unchanged. Model wording varies; the assertions are written to survive that and would be dishonest if they were not.

residual_policy.rule: A layer-0/2/4 case proves packaging and deterministic-helper parity for real; it does not prove that a model driving the adapter behaves identically. Cases that cannot close that gap declare it in a `residual:` line, and the runner reports RUNTIME_PROOF as not-run until layer 3 has actually executed.
residual_policy.what_layer_3_now_covers: The nine forward cases plus the two pre-existing in-case layer-3 blocks (emulate-routing-and-flags, msg-init-cto). Residuals attached to the remaining layer-0/2/4 cases are addressed by skill, not case-by-case: each skill's forward case exercises its routing, its ambiguity handling, its refusal and its safety gate against a live session.
